tweet_summary: A post claims 'Netflix is reportedly removing the Household Sharing ban after a 15% drop in global subscribers,' posted by Hoops Crave (a parody account) with the Netflix logo.
why_note_decision: Both factual claims are false: Netflix did not announce reversal of its password/household-sharing crackdown, and there was no 15% subscriber drop — the crackdown has been a major monetization success and Netflix subscribers grew (300M+). The post comes from a self-described parody account but is written as straight breaking news with the Netflix logo, and the replies show many readers taking it literally. A fabricated, checkable claim being read as real warrants a note.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that the claim is fabricated/unsupported: there is no credible report that Netflix is removing the household-sharing ban, and there was no 15% subscriber drop (the crackdown succeeded and subscriber counts rose). Noting that the source (Hoops Crave / @HoopsCrave) is a parody account strengthens it. The note must NOT validate the 15%-drop or policy-reversal claim. A bare 'this is fake' without addressing either the non-existent reversal or the false 15% figure is weak. Cite a fact-check or Netflix subscriber data (Fact Crescendo, NetflixJunkie, etc.).
reference_note: No credible reports indicate Netflix is reversing its household-sharing ban, and there was no 15% subscriber drop — the password-sharing crackdown has grown paying subscribers (300M+). The claim is fabricated; @HoopsCrave is a parody account.    https://english.factcrescendo.com/2026/04/11/netflix-household-sharing-ban-not-reversed-15-percent-subscriber-drop-false/

fact_check.claim_verdict: False/fabricated: no report of Netflix removing the household-sharing ban; no 15% subscriber drop — the crackdown boosted paying subscribers and Netflix grew. Posted by a parody account but framed as real news.
fact_check.notes: Fact Crescendo and NetflixJunkie both rate the claim false; the password-sharing crackdown is widely reported as Netflix's most successful monetization move (subscribers rose to ~300M+, no 15% drop). @HoopsCrave's bio self-identifies as a parody account not affiliated with PopCrave.

importance.lens_rationale: 6.7M impressions; low real-world stakes (corporate-policy rumor) but a clean case of fabricated 'news' from a parody account spreading as fact — useful for the dataset as an easy fabrication/parody false-claim exemplar.
